For iid weights equal to a>0 with probability p in (0,1) and b>a otherwise, suppose northeast directed bond percolation on the a-edges has positive forward survival probability theta(p). Then almost surely some global bi-infinite FPP geodesic exists. At the origin, forward and backward surviving-ray events depend on disjoint edge time levels and intersect with probability theta(p)^2. Their concatenation is monotone and every finite segment has Manhattan distance many a-edges, the minimum possible cost. Translation ergodicity upgrades positive probability of existence to probability one. This is a boundary obstruction to dropping nonatomicity, not a counterexample to the nonatomic-law target.
to_quote: Give each unoriented nearest-neighbor edge of Z^2 a finite nonnegative weight t_e, and let T(u,v) be the infimum of the weights of all finite walks from u to v, charging every edge traversal. A global bi-infinite geodesic is an injective adjacent-vertex sequence (v_k) indexed by all integers such that sum_{k=i}^{j-1} t_{v_k,v_{k+1}}=T(v_i,v_j) for every i<j. Competitors may leave any strip or region containing the sequence.

from_quote: DRAFT author derivation, independent review pending. In the constant weight-1 FPP environment, put f(k)=sign(k) floor(sqrt(abs(k))) for integers k, with f(0)=0. Join (k,f(k)) to (k+1,f(k)) horizontally and then move vertically at column k+1 to f(k+1). The resulting doubly infinite monotone staircase is a global geodesic: each finite segment has Manhattan-optimal length. Its two end directions are +e1 and -e1 because f(k)/abs(k) tends to zero, but neither tail lies eventually in any finite horizontal strip because f is unbounded at both ends. End directions alone therefore give no geometric finite-strip confinement. This example uses a constant law and does not refute a nonatomic iid theorem.

from_quote: An absence theorem restricted to bigeodesic tails in deterministic thin horizontal or vertical tubes requires a further confinement theorem, or an obstruction for wider and adaptive wandering, before it can establish unrestricted absence. Countable intersections over fixed finite widths do not cover a path whose transverse displacement is unbounded. A directional limit permits unbounded sublinear transverse displacement. The separate compactness route, taking limits of geodesics between opposite distant endpoints, likewise needs anchoring near a bounded region; endpoints on opposite sides alone allow the connecting paths to escape every fixed ball. These are missing bridge premises, not refutations of absence for nonatomic iid planar FPP.
